root_causes.description: product-catalog, a shared leaf dependency of frontend, checkout, and recommendation, is exhibiting saturated server-side p99 latency (~10000ms), which propagates as ~10s response times up the call graph to its callers. Resource usage and pod health are normal, consistent with an injected latency fault.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99 < 10 ms for a healthy leaf service

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000.000 ms — frontend caller of product-catalog saturated

evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU anomaly detected during window

root_causes.description: product-catalog shows sustained CPU consumption up to ~2.15 cores with p95=2.12, which could throttle request handling and inflate p99 latency; however the anomaly detector did not flag it, making this a secondary suspect.

evidence.expected_baseline: no anomaly detected; low steady-state CPU expected for Go product-catalog

root_causes.description: checkout's p99 is saturated at ~10000ms because it synchronously depends on product-catalog (along with frontend and recommendation). This is downstream propagation of the product-catalog latency rather than an independent checkout fault.

evidence.observed_value: Only a normal Scheduling event for product-catalog; no OOMKilled/BackOff restart events

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog pod network/response behavior for injected latency (e.g. tc netem / latency sidecar) and remove the latency fault on product-catalog.
Restart/roll the product-catalog deployment to clear a stuck latency condition; confirm p99 returns to sub-100ms.
Verify frontend, checkout, and recommendation p99 recover once product-catalog latency normalizes, confirming downstream propagation.
Add caching, request hedging, or circuit-breaker timeouts on product-catalog callers (frontend, checkout, recommendation) to reduce blast radius of a slow shared dependency.
If CPU is found throttled, raise product-catalog CPU limits/requests or scale replicas horizontally.
